newsitem.title: USA: US SPOT NATGAS PRICES ERASE GAINS AHEAD OF WEEKEND.
newsitem.headline: US SPOT NATGAS PRICES ERASE GAINS AHEAD OF WEEKEND.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices were on the retreat Friday following a week of significant gains as the futures market ended its rally and buyers shied away from the market ahead of the weekend, traders said.
NYMEX's September contract soared to a new high of $2.515 on Thursday before sliding to a low of $2.375 today.
On the Louisiana Gulf Coast, swing prices at the Henry Hub were quoted down an average of 12-15 cents to about $2.34-2.42, still carrying about a 10-cent premium to week-ago levels.

In the Midwest, swing prices lost 17 cents to the mid-$2.20s, also still about 10 cents above week-ago levels. Chicago city-gate gas prices were quoted at $2.43-2.48, down about 15 cents from Thursday.
In the Permian Basin market, prices defied the continuing heat in the West by falling 22 cents to $2.20-2.27, down from Thursday's highs around $2.50.
San Juan basin gas was also much lower in the low-$2.20s, while southern California border prices dove 24 cents to the high-$2.30s.
In the East, prices at the New York city gate erased Thursday's gains to land in the low-$2.50s.

Forecasts are calling for warmer weather across the Northeast, Midwest and southern plains this weekend, but cooler air is expected to return to Texas early next week, according to Weather Services Corp.
